acceptance.given: Repair work is executed against the frozen repository checkout and its tracked repository-relative paths.

oracle.expected: The S6 test compares the pre-repair and post-repair repository-relative path sets and reports them unchanged.
forbidden: Any repository-relative path is renamed, relocated, or rewritten.
A path comparison is omitted or replaced by filename-only inspection.
oracle.observable: The S6 test result contains an explicit before/after repository-relative path comparison with equal sets.

acceptance.then: The path comparison is evaluated after repair authoring and before acceptance.

failure_intents.selector_intent: S6 test fails when any repository-relative path differs between pre-repair and post-repair snapshots.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or preserve an S6 comparison proving repository-relative paths are byte-for-byte unchanged across repair; no path relocation or rewriting is permitted.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema or runtime-state change; revert only the path-comparison implementation and its test.

slice_hint.state_transition: Pre-repair path snapshot -> repair -> post-repair path comparison -> unchanged verdict.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: S6 comparison passes only when the complete repository-relative path set is unchanged.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result has reached success and includes its target, validator, command, probe, consumer, snapshot, and authority bindings.

oracle.expected: The S7 replay test independently verifies the produced output and records that verification in the successful Replay Result.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result is accepted without an independent output check.
The replay merely echoes its own success marker as output proof.
oracle.observable: The successful result contains an independently computed output verification record tied to the replay identity.

acceptance.then: The independent output verification is evaluated before the successful Replay Result is published.

failure_intents.selector_intent: S7 replay test produces RED when output verification is absent, self-referential, or not recorded in the successful result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure successful replay publication performs an independent output verification and persists its proof alongside the Replay Result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Replay result schema remains compatible; rollback removes only the independent-output verification wiring.

slice_hint.state_transition: Replay execution -> output independently recomputed -> verification bound to result -> success publication.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A Replay Result is successful only when an independent output verification record is present and valid.

acceptance.given: An external process is launched through the Toolchain process execution path with a configured finite time budget.

oracle.expected: The S30 execution test observes that the process either terminates normally or is stopped when the configured finite limit is reached, and records a deterministic terminal outcome.
forbidden: The process remains running beyond its configured finite limit.
Budget exhaustion is reported as successful completion.
oracle.observable: The S30 result contains the configured limit, observed termination or stop, and terminal status.

acceptance.then: The finite-time enforcement and terminal classification are evaluated after the external-process invocation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: S30 test fails when process_executor_v2 permits execution past the configured finite time limit.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a finite execution deadline for each external process and classify timeout or budget exhaustion as unsuccessful deterministic termination.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing process result fields; revert only deadline enforcement and terminal classification changes.

slice_hint.state_transition: Process launch -> bounded execution -> normal completion or enforced stop -> deterministic terminal result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The process result is terminal within the configured finite limit; exhaustion cannot yield success.

acceptance.given: An aggregate execution is launched through the same bounded Toolchain process/replay path with a configured finite time limit.

oracle.expected: The S30 aggregate execution test observes aggregate completion or enforced stop within the configured finite limit and records budget exhaustion as unsuccessful.
forbidden: The aggregate runs beyond its configured finite time limit.
Aggregate timeout is treated as a successful terminal result.
oracle.observable: The S30 result identifies the aggregate invocation, configured limit, observed stop or completion, and unsuccessful status on exhaustion.

acceptance.then: The aggregate deadline and terminal classification are evaluated after aggregate execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: S30 test fails when aggregate orchestration bypasses the finite process budget or marks budget exhaustion successful.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Apply the same finite deadline and deterministic unsuccessful-on-exhaustion rule to aggregate orchestration and its constituent process execution.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No aggregate schema change; revert only shared deadline propagation and terminal classification.

slice_hint.state_transition: Aggregate launch -> bounded child/process execution -> aggregate completion or enforced stop -> deterministic terminal result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The aggregate reaches a terminal result within the finite limit, with exhaustion classified unsuccessful.
